clue.text: The standard way to keep maximal speed in a manner of speaking

parts.note: par is the standard or norm, as in golf

indicators.note: the way is to hold the speed symbol within it, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a lane is a way or narrow road
c is the physicists' symbol for the speed of light, the greatest speed possible

explanation.surface: A rule about how to stay within the top speed limit, told in a roundabout way.
explanation.walkthrough: C, the speed of light, is the physicist's universal speed limit, which is why 'maximal speed' gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular idiom or way of talking, so it is a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Chum facing hell, a trial without end, quivers

parts.note: a chum is a pal, a friend
the pit is a name for hell

indicators.note: the closing letter of the word for a trial is dropped, leaving it without its end

parts.note: a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A friend facing a hellish ordeal that never ends is left trembling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without end' takes the last T off TEST, leaving TES.
explanation.definitionFit: To palpitate is to throb or flutter, so the verb matches quivers in sense and tense.

clue.text: Pride — is it hurt with bod finally becoming this?

definitions.text: Pride — is it hurt with bod finally becoming this?

indicators.note: only the closing letter of bod is taken
the letters of these words are damaged and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether wounded pride leaves a person feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hurt' rearranges PRIDEISIT, after D, the last letter of 'bod' signalled by 'finally'. The whole clue also defines: hurt pride leaves a bod downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose pride is wounded is left dejected, low in spirits.

clue.text: Repeatedly an hour late, say?

definitions.meaning: being an hour late is being past the set hour, one hour beyond another

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means again and again; whimsically, arriving an hour late is turning up at a time following the appointed one.

clue.text: See 5
Retail outlets with more than one floor not unknown

indicators.note: the letter for the unknown is to be taken away, it is not there

parts.note: storeys are the floors of a building, plural
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Shops occupying several levels, described as not unfamiliar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes Y (an algebra unknown) from STOREYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stores are shops, places where goods are sold to the public.

clue.text: Water plants — only 75% surviving in disaster

indicators.note: three quarters of the eight-letter word for disaster remains, so its final two letters are lost

parts.note: a calamity is a disaster

explanation.surface: Only a quarter of the aquatic flora perished in a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: CALAMITY has eight letters; keeping 75% leaves the first six. Calami is the plural of calamus, the sweet flag, a reed of wet ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The calamus or sweet flag is a marsh plant, so its plural names water plants.

clue.text: At home with computers etc I had to start

parts.note: in means at home
IT, information technology, covers computers and the like
had, as in had a meal, means ate

explanation.surface: Someone who works from home on computers needed to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate is to begin or set something going, a synonym of start.

clue.text: Cleric to bow in special prayer

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other
the word prayer is made into a special, unusual arrangement

parts.note: to bend is to bow

explanation.surface: A churchman stooping during a particular prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' scrambles the prayer's letters to PREARY before the bow goes in; a prebend is a cathedral stipend.
explanation.definitionFit: A prebendary is a canon who holds a prebend, a stipend from a cathedral, so he is a cleric.

clue.text: See 10
Judge again to receive commendation

parts.note: to reap is to receive or gain
praise is commendation

explanation.surface: A second assessment brings someone a reward of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappraise is to assess anew, to make a fresh judgement.

clue.text: See 4
The cranky suppose odd psychic projections will form

indicators.note: cranky means awry or eccentric, so the letters go out of order

explanation.surface: Eccentric people imagine that strange spiritual emanations will appear.
explanation.definitionFit: In spiritualism, pseudopods are limbs of ectoplasm said to reach out from a medium.

clue.text: Officer has new idea — to go Awol

indicators.note: the letters of idea are formed anew

parts.note: to decamp is to leave suddenly, like a soldier absent without leave

explanation.surface: An officer has a fresh idea: desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges IDEA as AIDE. Awol is military slang for absent without leave.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide-de-camp is a military officer serving as a general's assistant.

clue.text: Attended certain races and lost everything?

definitions.meaning: attended greyhound racing, a night at the track

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means deteriorated badly; literally it describes a trip to greyhound racing, where gamblers can lose all.

clue.text: See 17
See 17
Laggards struggling to be in top gear

indicators.note: struggling means in a mess, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Slowcoaches labour to get into high gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges LAGGARDS. 'top gear' is not a car's gear but best clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags are one's best clothes, the finest outfit or gear.

clue.text: Looked at non-pro team getting embarrassed

parts.note: con is the opposite of pro, as in pros and cons
a side is a team
red-faced, blushing

explanation.surface: Watched an amateur team that ended up red-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-pro' looks like amateur but means CON, the opposite of pro.
explanation.definitionFit: Considered means thought about or examined, a synonym of looked at.

clue.text: Turn towards bishop in public

indicators.note: the letter is put inside the word for public

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.definitionFit: To obvert is to turn something so its other face is presented towards the viewer.

definitions.text: in danger of being shot down
definitions.meaning: in the trenches of the First World War soldiers climbed out to attack under fire

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means going too far; literally it is climbing out of a trench into enemy fire.

See 4

A river bird joining a jolly lot having intimate contact

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for river on maps
the mina or myna is an Asian bird of the starling family
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Walking linked by a river, a bird joining a happy crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, RM.

clue.text: Lady protecting silver from harm

indicators.note: the lady surrounds the silver, guarding it within

parts.note: a dame is a titled lady
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A noblewoman guards her silverware from injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady' looks like the definition at the start, but the definition is 'harm' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage is injury or impairment, a synonym of harm.
